question_text: Explain why a supervised obstacle classifier with very high accuracy on its training images from a single simulator may still perform poorly on real road images. Relate your answer to overfitting and evaluation.
adaptation_rationale: Narrow simulation concern to supervised-model overfitting and unseen-condition evaluation. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: It may fit simulator-specific textures or lighting rather than general obstacle features. Real cameras/weather produce unseen examples, so apparent training success does not show generalization. Evaluate on separate representative real-world data; a large training/test performance gap suggests overfitting and motivates changing model complexity or tuning with validation data.

marking_points.criterion: Real images differ in relevant features/conditions.
Training accuracy alone does not establish performance on unseen data.
Independent representative evaluation and performance comparison can expose poor generalization.
